notes: Check batch 2026-10-29-check: four skill runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), no Opus, so the opus tier is unavailable in per_rule. All have rc 0, head 6d3eb7f, uncommitted true and skill_hash ca223bafe67c954b0dad03539f4c31d7117b6a72a913b38de55b05cd51cbe735, which equals evals/tools/common.py folder_hash of the working tree's idiomatic-elixir/. Each model_id matches its tier; the only other model name in each transcript is one claude-opus-5-5, the tool-definition model option noted in earlier check batches. Every transcript contains this round's new phrases ("or a trailing keyword list", "A pipeline never sits on one line", "in that order and each used once", "A `for` always takes"), so every run read the working-tree SKILL.md. Reads: all four SKILL.md, processes.md and ecto-phoenix.md; Expected reads (processes.md) is met in all four. Every session ran mix format --check-formatted itself.

Changed rules: git diff d04061d -- idiomatic-elixir/ adds the committed rule "Break a `->` clause whose pattern and body together pass 70 characters" and, uncommitted, rewords "Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call", the `do:` rule, the first pipeline bullet and the capture rule, adds the elem/2 sentence to "Match every expected shape and let unexpected ones crash", and turns the Bucket example in processes.md ("Keep each process behind one module") and the Module.concat example in macros.md into do-blocks. The text of the processes.md rules is unchanged. Of the listed rules, only the named-argument rule and the `->` rule changed; the other nine are graded to the standard of sweeps/2026-10-23/grades/rate-limiter-skill.json and rate-limiter-baseline.json, and the `->` rule to the standard of sweeps/2026-10-23-check-3/grades/rate-limiter-skill.json.

Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call, 0 of 4, graded against the current text. Deciding sentences per run: haiku-1, the opening sentence "Unless a call's result is bound to a name, each of its arguments is a name, a short literal, or a trailing keyword list" (no argument spans several lines); haiku-2, "A shorter literal that fits its line stays on one line." (line 92, five ETS options on one 98-character line, then :ets.new(name, table_options)); sonnet-1, the opening sentence's "a short literal" (lines 114-115, two four-element :ets.new/2 option lists inline on one line, 82 and 84 characters); sonnet-2, "A call whose result is bound to a name may take its options inline" and "A keyword list that is the call's last argument stays inline, one option per line" (lines 80-85, Keyword.validate!/2), with its five ETS options named one per line at lines 121-127 because one line would be 110 characters. The more-than-six-elements sentence is not triggered: no run has a literal of more than six elements. No run passes a multi-line map or struct to a call. The check-6 failure shape, :ets.new/2 options inline across several lines, appears in no run.

Break a `->` clause whose pattern and body together pass 70 characters, 0 of 4; exercised in haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2, not exercised in haiku-1, which has no case, cond, with ... else or receive in code. Deciding sentences: "A clause of `case`, `cond`, `with ... else` or `receive` stays on one line while its pattern, the `->` and its body together fit in 70 characters, not counting indentation." and "Once one clause breaks, `mix format` moves every clause's body down and separates the clauses with a blank line; keep that layout, and do not pull the short clauses back onto one line." The longest one-line clauses in code are sonnet-2 line 180 (57), sonnet-1 line 150 (52) and haiku-2 line 85 (47). The one close call: sonnet-1's moduledoc Oban example keeps {:error, {:rate_limited, retry_after_ms}} -> {:snooze, div(retry_after_ms, 1000) + 1} on one line (line 57, 85 characters) beside a one-line :ok clause. Following 2026-10-23-check-2 and check-3, which did not count clauses inside @moduledoc examples, it is not counted; counting it makes sonnet-1 violated and the count 1 of 4. Every other doc case with a long clause is broken with blank lines between clauses.

The other reworded rules, which this case does not list, were checked as other_violations. Pipeline one-line sentence ("A pipeline never sits on one line, however short"): 1 of 4, sonnet-1 line 162 (oldest = name |> :ets.select(match_spec) |> Enum.min(fn -> now end)); the other pipelines (haiku-1 lines 120-123 and 130-133, sonnet-1 lines 137-140) are multi-line and start with the value. `do:` rule: 0 of 4; the code's do: bodies are a call (haiku-1 line 158) and tuples (haiku-2 line 144, sonnet-2 line 200), with no fn or call-carrying capture on a do: line, no if ..., do: ..., else: and no for. Capture placeholder-order sentence: 0 of 4; the only captures are haiku-1 line 151, &(now - &1 < @window_ms), one placeholder used once and not counted under the captures rule, as the same capture was not in 2026-10-23, and haiku-2 line 137, &limit_entry/1. The elem/2 sentence: 0 of 4, no run calls elem/2.

Standard carried over: an if on one boolean condition is clean; a two-step with whose body returns a third fallible call is not counted (sonnet-2 lines 171-173); a run with no with and only raising boot-time calls is not exercised under the with rule (haiku-1, sonnet-1), and a single fallible call handled with case is clean (haiku-2, as 2026-10-22-check-6 haiku-2); all counts behind GenServer.call violate Pick the abstraction and Use ETS (haiku-1, as 2026-10-23 haiku-1); reading the limits file in init/1 is a missed case check but decides no verdict; key, object, rows, config and decoded are not counted under Naming; callers and child lists in @moduledoc count as the run's caller and supervision examples; a Jason compile warning from Jason not being installed is recorded in checks only (haiku-1, as 2026-10-22-check-6 and check-10).

Judgment calls: haiku-1 line 149 (# Timestamps are kept newest first, so the oldest one is last.) states an ordering the code relies on at line 111 and that the filter under it does not show, so Comments is clean, where 2026-10-23 haiku-1's comment over its filter restated it. Sonnet-1 line 142's Enum.map(users, fn {user_id, limit} -> {user_id, limit} end) is counted under "Use the `Enum` or `Map` function made for the job" because it is Map.to_list/1 written by hand, though the rule's table does not list that pair; drop it if the table is read as the whole rule. Sonnet-1 line 168 builds an atom, :"#{name}_limits", for its second table on every check; it is not counted under "Never build atoms for process names from runtime data" because the name comes from the start option, not request data, and names a table, not a process.

Designs. Haiku-1 keeps every count in one GenServer: check/2 is GenServer.call(server, {:check, to_string(user_id)}) and handle_call/3 keeps per-user timestamp lists, with a one-minute sweep. Haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 keep one ETS row per admitted request in a public table owned by a GenServer (a bag in haiku-2, an ordered_set in the Sonnet runs); the caller inserts its row, counts, and deletes the row when over; a handle_info/2 sweep deletes expired rows. Limits live in :persistent_term (haiku-2, sonnet-2) or a second protected ETS table (sonnet-1). Haiku-2 evaluates an Elixir-term limits file with Code.eval_file/1 and refuses users missing from it; the others read JSON with a default limit. Sonnet-1 accepts only string IDs (is_binary guard, line 94) while its moduledoc plug passes conn.assigns.current_user.id as is. Every run reads its limits file inside init/1.

Verification, in scratch copies under grade-scratch-2026-10-29/rate-limiter. All four pass mix format --check-formatted and none has a line over 98 characters. Haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 compile with elixirc --warnings-as-errors (Elixir 1.20.3, OTP 29); haiku-1 prints one warning, Jason.decode!/1 undefined (line 132), and compiles with a Jason stub over JSON.decode!/1.
